newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African vehicle hijackings double in a year.
newsitem.headline: S.African vehicle hijackings double in a year.

text.p: The rate of vehicle hijacking, the trademark crime of post-apartheid South Africa, was dramatically up with as many hijackings in the first half of this year as the whole of 1995, according to figures released in parliament on Wednesday.

Figures released by policing minister Sydney Mufamadi showed 8,316 vehicle hijackings countrywide in the first six months of 1996, compared to 8,350 in the whole of last year. Most hijackings were reported in Gauteng, the industrial heartland including Johannesburg, where 5,103 cases were reported in the first half of this year. In 1995 a total of 5,687 cases were reported.
Figures showed South Africa's murder rate dropped to an average of 1,949 a month in the first half of 1996, from last year's average of 2,243 a month.
Mufamadi recently declared hijacking a national priority crime and police have claimed significant successes against hijacking syndicates.
Opposition liberal Democratic Party spokesman DOuglas Gibson said the apparent doubling came despite a reported police crackdown.
"This situation cannot be tolerated. There must be harsh sentences for those who are convicted and this must include long terms of imprisonment," he said.
